theater: 北印度旁遮普與犍陀羅

battle.name: 巴克特里亞對印度的擴張
battle.theater: 北印度旁遮普與犍陀羅
battle.brief: 公元前二世紀末，巴克特里亞王德米特里烏斯一世率軍越過興都庫什山，渡印度河，攻入孔雀王朝西北的健馱羅與旁遮普。遠征軍以二百頭象與攻城器械開路，卻因戰線過長、季風與山地限制、補給斷絕而崩潰，德米特里烏斯回國後不久失去王位。卡面長矛並未隨軍遠來，只是這場戰爭裡雙方共用的刺擊技術底層。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前二世紀末中亞與南亞之間的一場邊疆戰爭，交戰的一方是希臘化的巴克特里亞王國，一方是南印度的孔雀王朝。巴克特里亞方面：國土橫跨中亞南部的巴克（Balkh，即今阿富汗北部一帶）盆地與索格底亞（Sogdia，即今塔吉克與烏茲別克之間的澤拉夫尚河流域），是一個由馬其頓人與希臘化移民建立的國家；軍隊以馬其頓式方陣步兵為骨幹，騎兵的數量與質素在當時僅次於塞琉古與托勒密，國王直接統率的禁衛步兵與伙伴騎兵是精銳核心，地方兵源則由巴克特里亞、索格底亞與大月氏邊境部族分頭提供。印度方面：孔雀王朝在難陀王朝末期仍號稱囊括自阿富汗南部至恆河中下游的廣土，軍隊以步兵弓手、近身短兵器與象兵為主，國王居中坐鎮，前線由各行省總督與城市聯盟分區防守，國都華氏城（Pataliputra）與北方要塞犍陀羅（Taxila）之間靠驛傳與河流維繫。第三方並非中立：西邊的塞琉古王國與南邊的安息都在同一時期向巴克特里亞施壓；大月氏棲居在更北面的天山一線，其後裔建立的貴霜王朝在兩個多世紀後接手了同一片土地。整場衝突因此不是兩個國家之間的單純決鬥，而是中亞、南亞與西亞三個勢力圈在同一條邊境線上的角力。
countriesEn: This was a frontier war fought in the late second century BC between Central and South Asia. On one side stood the Hellenistic Bactrian kingdom, on the other the Mauryan Empire of southern India. The Bactrian side: its territory ran across the basin of Bactra (Balkh, in the far north of present-day Afghanistan) and Sogdia (the Zeravshan valley between modern Tajikistan and Uzbekistan), a state built by Macedonians and Greek settlers. Its army had the Macedonian phalanx for a skeleton, and in the number and quality of its cavalry it ranked second only to the Seleucids and the Ptolemies; the heart of the force was the royal guard infantry and the Companion cavalry under the king's own command, while the manning came locally from Bactria, from Sogdia and from the tribes along the Yuezhi frontier. The Indian side: under the last Nanda dynasty the Mauryan Empire still claimed a vast territory running from southern Afghanistan to the middle and lower Ganges; its army was built on infantry archers, close-combat blades and war elephants, with the king in the centre, the front divided among provincial governors and city alliances, and the capital at Pataliputra tied to the northern stronghold of Taxila by courier posts and river transport. The third parties were not neutral. The Seleucid kingdom in the west and the Parthians in the south were both pressing on Bactria in these same years, while the Yuezhi, settled further north along the Tian Shan, would have their Kushan descendants take over the same ground more than two centuries later. The conflict was therefore not a simple duel between two states but a trial of strength between three spheres of power along one frontier line.
people: 留下姓名的有五位。巴克特里亞王德米特里烏斯一世（Demetrius I），歐提德莫斯一世之子，公元前二世紀末至前一世紀初在位，是這場遠征的統帥：普魯塔克《德米特里烏斯傳》記他娶了塞琉古王安條克二世之女亞歷山德拉，又把自己的女兒嫁給長子阿伽托克勒斯，用婚姻把巴克特里亞與塞琉古王室綁在一起。他同時在印度用兵、又在中亞的塞琉古內戰中押注，結果兩線皆敗。老王歐提德莫斯一世的事蹟在尤斯丁（Justin）《史記綱要》第十一卷有生動記述：塞琉古三世兵臨巴克特里亞城下時，老王把自己的坐騎讓給兒子德米特里烏斯，令其出城迎敵。印度方面最關鍵的名字是難陀王朝末代國王婆利鴆羅（Brihadratha）：相傳他被將軍普希亞密特拉（Pushyamitra）暗殺，後者另立政權建立巽伽王朝，《摩奴法典》與後出的編年史《Yupurana》都記下這段弒君與篡位。接下來幾位巽伽君主中，阿耆尼密特拉（Agnimitra）的阿拉哈巴德石柱銘文保存了最關鍵的一條戰爭記錄：銘文提到依萬那王（Yavana-rāja）曾圍攻娑迦多（Saketa，即今錫亞爾科特）與中大割（Madhyamika）等地，瓦蘇密特拉（Vasumitra）則在信度河擊潰依萬那騎兵。必須說清楚的是，這條銘文的年代在前一百四十年代，記的是後來梅安德羅的進攻，不是德米特里烏斯這一次；它的價值在於印證希臘人確實曾打到恆河一線。最後一位是梅安德羅（Menander），相傳即中國文獻中的遮留王，《大唐西域記》述犍陀羅（呾叉始羅）時提到此人；巴利文的《彌蘭陀問經》記他與比丘那先的問答，說明這位希臘君主治理之下的印度西北部，已經是一個有佛教信仰與學術傳統的社會。
peopleEn: Five names matter. Demetrius I, king of Bactria, son of Euthydemus I, reigned in the late second and early first centuries BC and commanded this expedition: Plutarch's Life of Demetrius records that he married Alexander, the daughter of the Seleucid king Antiochus II, and gave his own daughter in marriage to his elder son Agathocles, binding Bactria to the Seleucid court by marriage. He campaigned in India and staked his fortunes in the Seleucid civil war in Central Asia at the same time, and lost on both fronts. The doings of the old king Euthydemus I are vividly preserved in Book XI of Justin's Epitome: when Seleucus III brought his army up to the walls of Bactria, the old man gave his own horse to his son Demetrius and sent him out to meet the enemy. On the Indian side the crucial name is the last Nanda king, Brihadratha: by tradition he was murdered by his general Pushyamitra, who founded a new dynasty, the Shunga line, and both the Manusmriti and the later chronicle known as the Yupurana record this regicide and usurpation. Among the Shunga rulers who followed, the Allahabad pillar inscription of Agnimitra preserves the single most important record of fighting on this frontier: it names a Yavana king who besieged Saketa, the modern Sialkot, and Madhyamika, and it credits Vasumitra with destroying Yavana cavalry on the Sindhu river. It has to be said plainly that this inscription dates to the 140s BC and refers to the later offensive of Menander, not to the campaign of Demetrius; its value lies in confirming that Greek troops did reach the Ganges line. The last name is Menander, held to be the ruler called Zheliuwang in Chinese sources, mentioned in the Great Tang Records on the Western Regions in its account of Taxila; the Pali Milindapanha sets down his questions to the monk Nagasena, showing that the north-west of India under this Macedonian king was already a society with Buddhist belief and scholarly tradition.
kits: 先說清楚一件事：卡面上的這把埃及長矛並沒有隨巴克特里亞大軍出現在印度。埃及長矛是早王朝時期（約公元前三千二百年）的兵器，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上，是尼羅河谷守城與列陣所用的樸素長柄刺器；到希臘化時代，同一支東方式的矛兵早已改頭換面。但把它放進這場戰爭的裝備表仍有理由：巴克特里亞軍中方陣矛兵所用的長矛（sarissa，即腓力二世改革後的長柄刺器，約四米至六米，配重尾栓插地撐住方陣），與印度步兵手中以竹木為杆、綁上青銅或鐵矛頭的刺器、以及土邦象兵所用的象鏢，在構造原理上同屬「金屬矛頭加長杆」這一系；埃及長矛正是這條技術譜系上最早的定形樣本，可以當作三千年後印度河平原上那些矛陣的祖型來看。就這場戰爭本身的實際配置而言，狄奧多羅斯《歷史》第二卷第三十九章留下了一份極為罕見的軍備清單：步軍二萬、騎軍一萬、二百頭象、一千具弩砲、五百張複合弓、二百張大型弓、戰車二百輛、帶鐮刀的戰車一千輛、以騾牽引的戰車五百輛，另有若干攻城機。這份清單說明的是巴克特里亞把希臘化的攻城技術、中亞的騎兵與印度的象兵編在同一支軍隊裡。防護上，希臘方陣用重盔配方陣盾（thorax）與小圓盾（pelta），印度步兵則多用木盾、弓與輕甲；弓的形制兩邊都能見到，但印度的弓更短、箭鏃更多樣。印度方面真正獨特的是披甲大象、象鏢與投石索手。運輸靠牛車、騾車與馭象，沒有大型攻城塔，卻有可以對付城牆的扭力弩砲與撞槌；後勤線自巴克（Balkh）經瓦罕走廊與興都庫什山的巴米揚谷地南下，再沿庫什河谷到印度河上游的烏迪（Ohind，阿托克附近）渡口，全程約一千六百公里。
kitsEn: One thing must be said at the outset: the Egyptian spear on the card did not march into India with the Bactrian army. The Egyptian spear belongs to the Old Kingdom, to about 3200 BC, a plain hafted thrusting weapon with a copper or bronze head bound to a wooden shaft, used by the Nile valley to hold ramparts and to fight in line; by Hellenistic times the eastern spear line had been transformed many times over. There is still a reason for placing it in the equipment table of this war. The long pike of the Bactrian phalanx, the sarissa introduced by Philip II and running roughly four to six metres, with its weighted butt-spike planted in the ground to hold the line together, the bamboo-and-wood spears with bronze or iron heads carried by Indian infantry, and the elephant goads of the Indian war elephants all belong to a single technical family, metal head on a long shaft, and the Egyptian spear is the earliest fixed form of that family. It can be read as the ancestor type of the spear lines that would stand on the plains of the Indus three thousand years later. For the actual order of battle in this war, Diodorus in the second book of his History, chapter 39, has left a remarkably detailed inventory: twenty thousand foot, ten thousand horse, two hundred elephants, a thousand catapults, five hundred composite bows, two hundred large bows, two hundred chariots, a thousand scythed chariots, five hundred mule-drawn chariots, together with siege machinery. The point of that list is that Bactria marched with Hellenistic siegecraft, Central Asian cavalry and Indian elephants in a single army. In armour the Greek phalanx used heavy helmets with the thorax and the small round pelta, while Indian foot leaned on wooden shields, the bow and light body armour; the bow existed on both sides, but the Indian bow was shorter and its arrowheads more varied. What was genuinely Indian was the armoured elephant, the goad and the slingers. Transport rested on ox carts, mule carts and elephants; there were no great siege towers, but there were torsion catapults and battering rams for the walls. The line of supply ran from Balkh through the Wakhan corridor and the Bamiyan valley of the Hindu Kush, then down the Kush valley to the crossing at Ohind, near Attock, on the upper Indus, about sixteen hundred kilometres in all.
tactics: 這場遠征的戰術可以拆成五步。第一步是集結與越嶺：軍隊自巴克盆地出發，經索格底亞東緣循瓦罕走廊越過興都庫什山的高山隘口；山口的冬令積雪與深谷迫使車隊與象群分批輕裝通過，行程因此拉長，後方與本國的聯繫也隨之變薄。第二步是渡河與攻取節點城市：印度河上游可通行的渡口在烏迪一帶，過河後兵鋒指向犍陀羅與健馱羅（Gandhara）平原上的城邑；印度城邑多有土築或木柵的圍牆與環壕，希臘人靠扭力弩砲、撞槌與攻城塔壓制，狄奧多羅斯清單裡的一千具弩砲正是為攻堅而備。第三步是會戰：最常見的組合是以象兵在正面展開，希臘方陣與重騎在側翼待命；希臘人的戰術傳統是用方陣正面抵住象群衝鋒，側翼以輕裝部隊投射火力，待象群亂後再以騎兵衝擊，但印度方的象群在季風氣候下容易掉膘、腳傷，飼料供應亦難維持。第四步是包圍與游擊：孔雀王朝的地方總督與城市聯盟不與希臘人正面決鬥，而以輕騎切斷糧道、反覆襲擊攻城部隊的分隊；希臘軍深入之後糧秣只能就地徵發，一旦切斷了巴克方向來的補給線，縱深數百公里的戰線便撐不住。第五步是撤退：普魯塔克記載德米特里烏斯在一次大敗之後僅餘一匹騾子與一件襯衣，靠村落收留藏身；傳統的解釋是饑荒與戰敗同時壓上，巴克特里亞本地的糧食也因軍隊久駐而耗盡，撤退遂成為全軍的集體行動。整體而言，這是一場典型的遠征型攻勢作戰：以攻城器與象兵掩護長距離機動，最後敗在補給與距離，而不是敗在某一場會戰的正面交鋒。
tacticsEn: The operation can be broken into five stages. The first is concentration and the crossing of the mountains. The army set out from the basin of Bactra, skirted the eastern edge of Sogdia and climbed through the high passes of the Hindu Kush by way of the Wakhan corridor; winter snow in the passes and the depth of the valleys forced the wagons and the elephants to move in lightly loaded batches, which stretched the march and thinned the tie between the army and the country behind it. The second is the river crossing and the taking of the nodal cities. The workable fords on the upper Indus lay around Ohind, and once over the water the spearhead pointed at the settlements of the Taxila plain and of Gandhara. Indian towns were ringed with earthen or timber palisades and ditches, and the Greeks answered them with torsion catapults, rams and siege towers; the thousand catapults in Diodorus's inventory were exactly this kind of preparation. The third is the pitched battle. The commonest combination was the elephant line deployed in front, with the Greek phalanx and the heavy cavalry held on the flanks. The Greek tactical tradition was to absorb the charge of the elephants with the front of the phalanx, to put light troops on the flanks to shoot into the confusion, and then to charge with the cavalry once the elephants had broken; but Indian animals, in a monsoon climate, lost condition, went lame, and could not easily be fed. The fourth is siege and harassment. The provincial governors and city alliances of the Mauryan state did not meet the Greeks in the open; they cut the supply lines with light cavalry and returned again and again to strike the isolated detachments at the siege works. Once the Greek army had pushed inland its grain could only be taken from the country it occupied, and the moment the line of supply running back towards Balkh was cut, a front several hundred kilometres long could not be held. The fifth is the withdrawal. Plutarch records that after a great defeat Demetrius had nothing left but a mule and a shirt and was hidden by the people of a village; the traditional explanation is that famine and defeat came down together, that the food of Bactria itself was used up by a long-strung army, and that the withdrawal became the act of the whole force. In overall terms this was a typical expeditionary offensive: siegecraft and elephants used to cover a long movement, ending in supply and distance rather than in the frontal collision of any single battle.
data: 可以核對的數字分三類。第一類是古典作家留下的具體數目。狄奧多羅斯《歷史》第二卷第三十九章記載巴克特里亞王的印度遠征軍備：步兵二萬、騎兵一萬、戰象二百、弩砲一千、複合弓五百、大型弓二百、戰車二百、帶鐮刀的戰車一千、騾車五百，另有攻城用機；這份清單是古典文獻中關於希臘化軍備最詳細的一次自述，但它是兵種陳列，未必要同時在役。普魯塔克沒有給出德米特里烏斯的兵力數字，只記了大敗、失國與流亡的結局。斯特拉波《地理學》第十一卷則說德米特里烏斯征服了印度大片土地而終究喪失。尤斯丁《史記綱要》第十一卷提到德米特里烏斯死後，王國在他的諸子之間分裂，隨後安息王米特達梯斯一世消滅了狄奧多圖斯家的統治。第二類是考古與碑銘數字。巴基斯坦的塔克西拉與斯哈特沙赫布（Shahbaz Garhi）、坎大哈（Kandahar）的所謂希臘人城址，以及阿富汗艾-汗姆（Ai-Khanoum）城址，提供了印度河上游的城市規劃、貨幣與文字實物；艾-汗姆在二十世紀九十年代出土的希臘文與巴克特里亞文銘刻，證明這座城市在德米特里烏斯時期已經存在。阿拉哈巴德石柱銘文則是巽伽朝最重要的戰爭文獻。第三類是推估，必須打折：孔雀王朝的版圖一般估計在五百萬平方公里上下，涵蓋今巴基斯坦大部、阿富汗南部與印度北部至恆河中下游；人口估算自五千萬至一億以上不等，爭議頗大；遠征軍的實際作戰兵力，多數研究認為在數萬人上下，其中步兵為主，專業騎兵佔比不大；自巴克（Balkh）到犍陀羅的陸路約一千六百公里，越嶺段海拔在三千米上下。年代方面，通行說法把德米特里烏斯即位定在公元前二〇〇年前後、印度遠征定在前二〇〇至前一八〇年之間，巽伽王朝則始於前一百八十五至前一八〇年；學界對先後次序有不同排列，並無定論。本戰役的確切月份無文獻可考——普魯塔克只記事件次序而不記時令，古典作家通篇未提月份；卡面取四月，是沿用同一批無月份記載的古代戰爭的統一時令標示，不代表有精確日期的證據。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is what the classical writers set down in figures. Diodorus, second book, chapter 39, gives the inventory of the Bactrian king's expedition to India: twenty thousand foot, ten thousand horse, two hundred war elephants, a thousand catapults, five hundred composite bows, two hundred large bows, two hundred chariots, a thousand scythed chariots, five hundred mule-drawn carts, together with siege machinery. This is the fullest self-description of Hellenistic armament surviving in the classical literature, though it is a display of arms and need not have had all of it under arms at once. Plutarch gives no strength for Demetrius, only the defeat, the loss of the kingdom and the flight. Strabo, in the eleventh book of the Geography, says that Demetrius conquered a great part of India and in the end lost it. Justin's Epitome, book XI, records that after Demetrius's death the kingdom was divided among his sons, and that Mithridates I of Parthia afterwards destroyed the rule of the house of Diodotus. The second class is archaeological and epigraphic. Taxila in Pakistan, Shahbaz Garhi, the so-called Greek settlements of Kandahar, and the site of Ai-Khanoum in Afghanistan supply the physical evidence of town planning, coinage and writing on the upper Indus; the Greek and Bactrian inscriptions recovered at Ai-Khanoum in the 1990s establish that the city already existed in Demetrius's time. The Allahabad pillar inscription is the most important piece of Shunga-period waging documentation. The third class is estimate, and must be discounted: the Mauryan Empire is generally put at about five million square kilometres, covering most of modern Pakistan, southern Afghanistan and northern India down to the middle Ganges; estimates of its population run from fifty million to more than a hundred million and are much disputed; the actual field strength of the expedition is put by most studies in the tens of thousands, infantry for the most part, with the professional cavalry a small fraction; and the land route from Balkh to Taxila is about sixteen hundred kilometres, the mountain section running at heights around three thousand metres. As for dates, the usual reckoning places Demetrius's accession around 200 BC and the Indian expedition between 200 and 180 BC, while the Shunga dynasty begins in 185 or 180 BC; the order of events is arranged differently by different scholars and no consensus exists.
cause: 打起來的原因分四層。最表層是邊界上的摩擦：巴克特里亞的東界在印度河上游，而孔雀王朝的西北行省（健馱羅、犍陀羅、旁遮普）控制著印度河兩岸的關隘與城邑，兩國的牧場、稅關與商隊路線在同一條河上互相抵觸。第二層是孔雀王朝內部的危機：婆利鴆羅在位末期，宮廷與軍方的矛盾激化，總督與將軍手握重兵，終於在公元前一百八十五至一百八十年前後釀成普希亞密特拉的政變；王位更替使西北邊防空虛，正是外軍叩關的時機。第三層是德米特里烏斯本人的戰略處境：他必須同時面對西邊塞琉古王室的索求、南邊安息勢力的推進，以及本國在索格底亞的整合；往東推進、奪取印度河上游的富庶行省，既能擴大稅基，也能切斷安息與孔雀之間可能的聯手；娶安條克二世之女亞歷山德拉、與塞琉古結盟，正是為這場東征取得外交上的合法性，並取得攻城工程技術上的支援。第四層是技術與經驗的推力：塞琉古王國的攻城技術已經成熟，遠征不再是沒有器械的冒險；而馬其頓方陣兵在巴克特里亞本地兵源有限，擴軍的誘因強烈。於是公元前一百八十年前後，一支希臘化的大軍自中亞盆地跨過高山，向南亞的平原推了過去。
causeEn: The reasons run in four layers. The outermost is friction along the border. Bactria's eastern frontier lay on the upper Indus, while the north-western provinces of the Mauryan state, Gandhara, Taxila and the Punjab, held the crossings and the towns on both banks of the river; the pastures, the customs posts and the caravan roads of the two countries rubbed against each other along the same water. The second layer is the crisis inside the Mauryan state. In the last years of Brihadratha's reign the tension between the court and the command grew, governors and generals held armed power of their own, and this came to a head in the coup of Pushyamitra in about 185 or 180 BC. A change of dynasty left the north-west frontier thinly held, and that was the moment for an army from outside to knock on the gate. The third layer is Demetrius's own strategic position. He had to meet at once the demands of the Seleucid court in the west, the advance of the Parthians in the south, and the work of consolidating Sogdia at home. Pushing east and seizing the rich provinces of the upper Indus would enlarge his tax base and would cut off any possibility of a Parthian-Mauryan combination; marrying Alexander, the daughter of Antiochus II, and tying himself to the Seleucids was how he secured the diplomatic legitimacy for this eastern war and the siegecraft and engineers that came with it. The fourth layer is the pull of technique and experience. The Seleucid empire's siege technology had matured, so an expedition was no longer an adventure without engines; and the local manpower available for the Macedonian phalanx in Bactria was thin, which made expansion attractive. Thus, around 180 BC, a Hellenistic host crossed the high mountains out of the Central Asian basin and pushed down onto the plains of South Asia.
impact: 這場遠征的直接結果是失敗，但它留下的東西比勝仗更多。第一，希臘人在印度北部建立了持久的據點：犍陀羅、健馱羅平原與旁遮普一線出現了希臘式城鎮、希臘文與巴克特里亞字母的銘刻，以及以希臘王名號鑄行的雙語錢幣；此後梅安德羅所建的印度-希臘王國以娑迦多（Saketa，即今錫亞爾科特）為都，就是建立在這次遠征鋪開的網絡上。第二，藝術與宗教的接觸就此打開：犍陀羅與巴克特里亞一帶出現了把希臘式寫實人像與印度佛陀題材結合的雕塑，國際學術界一般稱之為犍陀羅藝術或希臘-佛教藝術；艾-汗姆出土的希臘式城市街區、劇院與體育設施，則是希臘化中亞的城市樣板。巴利文《彌蘭陀問經》記希臘王與比丘那先的問答，說明這位王室的統治已深到需要以佛法對話。第三，戰爭把依萬那（Yavana，希臘人）這個詞固定進了南亞的歷史記憶：梵文與普利亞語文獻中的依萬那王、依萬那騎兵、依萬那人的城市，至今仍指涉這批北來的征服者。第四，行政與歲紀制度的傳播：學界曾提出印度-希臘王可能使用過一種以希臘化王即位為起點的紀年，並認為後來的塞種紀、蘇利耶紀與傳統西元紀年的關係由此而來，雖然此說仍有爭議。第五，軍事上的示範：二百頭象加攻城器的遠征把多兵種合成作戰推到極限，也把季風、河流、高山與距離這四種限制，擺在後來所有北來征服者面前。
impactEn: The expedition failed, but what it left behind is worth more than a victory would have been. First, the Greeks established durable footholds in northern India. Along Taxila, the Gandhara plain and the Punjab there appeared Greek-style towns, inscriptions in Greek and in the Bactrian script, and bilingual coinage struck in the name of Greek kings; the Indo-Greek kingdom with Menander, based at Saketa, the modern Sialkot, was built on the network that this expedition opened. Second, the contact between art and religion was begun. In Gandhara and in Bactria there appeared sculpture that married the naturalistic Greek figure to Indian Buddhist subject matter, known in international scholarship as Gandharan art or Greek-Buddhist art; the Greek street plan, theatre and athletic installations excavated at Ai-Khanoum are the model of the Hellenistic city in Central Asia. The Pali Milindapanha, which sets down the questions put by a Greek king to the monk Nagasena, shows that the rule of this house had gone deep enough to want a debate with the Buddhist teaching. Third, the war fixed the word Yavana, the Greek, into the historical memory of South Asia: the Yavana king, the Yavana cavalry and the Yavana city in the Sanskrit and Pali texts still point at this band of northern conquerors. Fourth, the spread of administration and of era reckoning: it has been argued that the Indo-Greek kings may have used a year count reckoned from the accession of a Hellenistic king, and that the Saka era, the Sūrya era and the traditional reckoning of the common era stand in some relation to it, though the argument remains disputed. Fifth, a demonstration in war. An expedition of two hundred elephants and heavy siegecraft pushed combined-arms warfare to its limit, and set before every later conqueror from the north the same four constraints: the monsoon, the rivers, the mountains and the distance.
result: 公元前二世紀末的這場遠征以失敗收場。德米特里烏斯的大軍在印度河上游消耗殆盡：印度方面的巽伽朝廷在普希亞密特拉率軍平定西北之後，得以重新控制犍陀羅與健馱羅；希臘方面則傳出饑荒與大敗的消息，德米特里烏斯失去王位，據說在公元前一百八十年前後被暗殺，他的兩個兒子（其中一人是阿伽托克勒斯）爭奪殘餘的巴克特里亞。尤斯丁《史記綱要》第十一卷說得更冷：德米特里烏斯死後，王國在他的諸子之間分裂，隨後安息王米特達梯斯一世出兵，把狄奧多圖斯家族在巴克特里亞的統治徹底清除。留下的則是另一條線：巴克特里亞的希臘人並沒有從中亞消失，約一個半世紀後，梅安德羅（遮留王）在印度西北重建了以娑迦多為都的印度-希臘王國，並深入到恆河流域；這個王國又延續了一百多年，最後在公元前一世紀中期被巽伽與貴霜兩方面的力量擠壓，於是希臘化的巴克特里亞人從印度的政治地圖上退場。若把整件事連起來看，結果可以這樣概括：德米特里烏斯用一支足以攻城的遠征軍證明了希臘化國家可以打到印度，但巴克特里亞的國力不足以同時養住中亞的家業與南亞的戰場，於是一次成功的突破變成了漫長的消耗，最終以國王被弒、王國分裂、故土喪失收場；而它打開的那條通道，此後由梅安德羅、巽伽與貴霜一行人接力走完。
resultEn: The expedition of the late second century BC ended in failure. Demetrius's host was spent on the upper Indus. On the Indian side, once the Shunga court under Pushyamitra had pacified the north-west it was able to retake Taxila and Gandhara; on the Greek side came news of famine and of a great defeat, Demetrius lost his throne and was said to have been assassinated around 180 BC, and his two sons, one of them Agathocles, fought over what was left of Bactria. Justin's Epitome, book XI, puts it more coldly: after Demetrius's death the kingdom was divided among his sons, and then Mithridates I, king of the Parthians, marched in and destroyed the rule of the house of Diodotus in Bactria. What survived was a different line. The Greeks of Bactria did not vanish from Central Asia; about a century and a half later Menander, the Zheliuwang of the Chinese texts, rebuilt an Indo-Greek kingdom in the north-west of India with its capital at Saketa, and pushed down to the Ganges. That kingdom lasted for more than another century before it was squeezed by the Shungas on one side and the Kushans on the other, and the Hellenistic Bactrians left the political map of India. Taken as a whole, the result can be put this way. Demetrius proved with a siege-grade expeditionary army that a Hellenistic state could reach India, but the resources of Bactria were not enough to keep a household in Central Asia and a war in South Asia at the same time; a successful breakthrough turned into a long drain, and it ended with a king murdered, a kingdom split and the homeland lost. The corridor it opened was then walked the whole way by Menander, by the Shungas and by the Kushans in turn.
